release_history.managed_recipe:
# Managed JSON-dashboard host. Scenes remains an optional acceptance image.
FROM satorykono/bioetl-grafana-router7-canvas@sha256:835ae6710c16792906856230b017f25b95bac870ddcd1eb4b55542dfcea6d107
USER root
RUN rm -rf /usr/share/grafana/data/plugins-bundled/bioetl-scenes-app
USER grafana

compose.grafana/tooling/router-v7-bridge/compose:
# Explicit candidate opt-in on a separate acceptance host/database only.
# Merge with docker-compose.monitoring.yml; this is not the default runtime.
services:
  grafana:
    image: satorykono/bioetl-grafana-router7-canvas@sha256:835ae6710c16792906856230b017f25b95bac870ddcd1eb4b55542dfcea6d107
    environment:
      - GF_PLUGINS_ALLOW_LOADING_UNSIGNED_PLUGINS=bioetl-scenes-app,bioetl-selectorshell-panel

# Candidate overlay: use only with an isolated database before governed rollout.
services:
  grafana:
    image: satorykono/bioetl-grafana-router7-canvas@sha256:6663692079097edcdf9c4d3cdea12932c68f459ed0a7c5716c6fad3964ceae11
    environment:
      - GF_PLUGINS_ALLOW_LOADING_UNSIGNED_PLUGINS=bioetl-selectorshell-panel
compose.docker-compose.monitoring.yml:
name: bioetl-monitoring

# OPTIONAL operator stack (ADR-010). Not part of the default release bundle.
# Default local workflow: Python/venv only, or main stack alone.
# Removed from this surface: Loki, Promtail, Tempo, Quarantine Explorer.
#
# Local resource budget (32 GiB Windows hosts):
#   prometheus 3g + grafana 2g + renderer 3g + pushgateway 512m ≈ 8.5g cgroup caps
#   (was ~10g + 7.5g + 15g + 2.5g ≈ 35g — host thrash / OOM).

services:
  # Cap cgroup + TSDB retention so rule/dashboard peaks stay in-budget
  # (was mem_limit 10g with 8–10g peaks under recording-rule load).
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v3.13.1@sha256:3c42b892cf723fa54d2f262c37a0e1f80aa8c8ddb1da7b9b0df9455a35a7f893
    container_name: bioetl-prometheus
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:9090:9090"
    environment:
      # Soft Go heap cap under mem_limit 3g (was unbounded → 8–10g peaks / host thrash).
      - GOMEMLIMIT=${PROMETHEUS_GOMEMLIMIT:-2500MiB}
      - GOGC=${PROMETHEUS_GOGC:-50}
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./grafana/prometheus-rules:/etc/prometheus/rules:ro
      - prometheus-data:/prometheus
    command:
      - "--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml"
      - "--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus"
      - "--web.enable-admin-api"
      - "--storage.tsdb.retention.time=7d"
      - "--storage.tsdb.retention.size=2GB"
      # Local Desktop: fewer concurrent queries under rule load (was 4).
      - "--query.max-concurrency=2"
      - "--query.timeout=30s"
      - "--query.max-samples=5000000"
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD",
          "wget",
          "--quiet",
          "--tries=1",
          "--spider",
          "http://localhost:9090/-/healthy",
        ]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 15s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 60s
    networks:
      - monitoring
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Prefer killing renderer first (oom_score_adj 800); Prom is more valuable.
    oom_score_adj: 200
    mem_limit: 3g
    memswap_limit: 3g
    mem_reservation: 768m
    cpus: 2.0
    pids_limit: 2560
    init: true
    stop_grace_period: 120s
    logging:
      { driver: json-file, options: { max-size: "200m", max-file: "10" } }

  pushgateway:
    image: prom/pushgateway:v1.11.3@sha256:74fa117cef2d7e383112d25139ff1c2d2e309c35389a9e0554a47136a1482e48
    container_name: bioetl-pushgateway
    # Preserve completed CLI snapshots across container recreation.
    volumes:
      - pushgateway-data:/pushgateway
    command:
      - "--persistence.file=/pushgateway/metrics.db"
      - "--persistence.interval=30s"
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:9091:9091"
    networks:
      - monitoring
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD",
          "wget",
          "--quiet",
          "--tries=1",
          "--spider",
          "http://localhost:9091/-/healthy",
        ]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 15s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 60s
    mem_limit: 512m
    mem_reservation: 64m
    cpus: 0.5
    pids_limit: 512
    init: true
    stop_grace_period: 120s
    logging:
      { driver: json-file, options: { max-size: "100m", max-file: "10" } }

  grafana:
    image: satorykono/bioetl-grafana-router7-canvas@sha256:6663692079097edcdf9c4d3cdea12932c68f459ed0a7c5716c6fad3964ceae11
    container_name: bioetl-grafana
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:3000:3000"
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD:?GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD is required}
      - GF_PLUGINS_ALLOW_LOADING_UNSIGNED_PLUGINS=bioetl-selectorshell-panel
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
      - GF_METRICS_ENABLED=true
      - GF_LOG_LEVEL=info
      - GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=http://localhost:3000
      - GF_SERVER_SERVE_FROM_SUB_PATH=false
      # Operator-facing clock on all shipped dashboards: YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm
      # (Grafana uses mm for minutes). Applies to time picker, axis ticks,
      # and default Time fields. Panel units use the same custom format.
      - GF_DATE_FORMATS_FULL_DATE=YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm
      - GF_DATE_FORMATS_INTERVAL_SECOND=HH:mm:ss
      - GF_DATE_FORMATS_INTERVAL_MINUTE=YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm
      - GF_DATE_FORMATS_INTERVAL_HOUR=YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm
      - GF_DATE_FORMATS_INTERVAL_DAY=YYYY-MM-DD
      - GF_DATE_FORMATS_INTERVAL_MONTH=YYYY-MM
      - GF_DATE_FORMATS_INTERVAL_YEAR=YYYY
      - GF_DATE_FORMATS_USE_BROWSER_LOCALE=false
      # Required for BioETL Ops HTTP panels (Run Explorer, identity tables, etc.).
      # Infinity 3.8.0 is retained for the private Grafana 13.2.3 host. Keep this pin
      # until a newer plugin passes the Ops HTTP table render checks.
      - BIOETL_INFINITY_PLUGIN_VERSION=${BIOETL_INFINITY_PLUGIN_VERSION:-3.8.0}
      # Remote renderer is optional for UI. When renderer is down/OOM, Grafana must
      # fail screenshot/PDF calls quickly — not hang worker threads (was unbounded
      # wait against dead Chromium). Dashboards keep working without renderer.
      - GF_RENDERING_SERVER_URL=http://renderer:8081/render
      - GF_RENDERING_CALLBACK_URL=http://grafana:3000/
      - GF_RENDERING_RENDERER_TOKEN=${GF_RENDERING_RENDERER_TOKEN:?GF_RENDERING_RENDERER_TOKEN is required}
      # Bounded client timeout toward renderer. 20s aborted table d-solo (408/500)
      # while Chromium was still waiting on Live WS / query-ready. 60s matches
      # give-up-on-all-queries + readiness slack; still fail-closed vs unbounded.
      # Dead renderer: recover_renderer (do not restart Grafana).
      - GF_RENDERING_RENDERING_TIMEOUT=${GF_RENDERING_RENDERING_TIMEOUT:-60s}
      - GF_RENDERING_CONCURRENT_RENDER_REQUEST_LIMIT=${GF_RENDERING_CONCURRENT_RENDER_REQUEST_LIMIT:-1}
      # Control-plane HTTP helpers on main bioetl health server (not Quarantine Explorer).
      # IMPORTANT: do not export BIOETL_OPS_HTTP_URL= (empty) on the host — an empty
      # value wipes the compose default and provisions Infinity with url="".
      # Omit the var, or set a non-empty URL. Bootstrap also materializes a fallback.
      - BIOETL_OPS_HTTP_URL=${BIOETL_OPS_HTTP_URL:-http://bioetl:8000}
      # Expected runtime origin from runtime_manager (64-char hex). Bootstrap
      # provisions Ops HTTP only when /ops/control-plane/ready matches this id.
      # Default "unmanaged" → Prometheus-only (Grafana still starts). Set
      # BIOETL_GRAFANA_REQUIRE_OPS_HTTP=1 for audit/render fail-closed.
      - BIOETL_EXPECTED_RUNTIME_SOURCE_ID=${BIOETL_RUNTIME_SOURCE_ID:-unmanaged}
      - BIOETL_GRAFANA_REQUIRE_OPS_HTTP=${BIOETL_GRAFANA_REQUIRE_OPS_HTTP:-0}
      # Ops ready poll budget. Soft default is short (bootstrap uses 5×1s when
      # REQUIRE_OPS_HTTP=0) so a late bioetl does not delay Grafana ~60s and
      # thrash healthchecks. Fail-closed audit sets REQUIRE_OPS_HTTP=1 (30×2s).
      # Explicit host overrides still win via the same env names.
      - BIOETL_GRAFANA_OPS_READY_ATTEMPTS=${BIOETL_GRAFANA_OPS_READY_ATTEMPTS:-}
      - BIOETL_GRAFANA_OPS_READY_SLEEP_SEC=${BIOETL_GRAFANA_OPS_READY_SLEEP_SEC:-}
    volumes:
      - grafana-data:/var/lib/grafana
      - ./grafana/provisioning/datasources-core:/etc/bioetl-grafana/datasources-core:ro
      - ./grafana/scripts/bootstrap-datasources.sh:/usr/local/bin/bioetl-bootstrap-grafana.sh:ro
      # Bootstrap selects exactly one provider: full dashboards only after
      # managed Ops HTTP identity, otherwise same-UID static notices.
      - ./grafana/provisioning/dashboards:/etc/bioetl-grafana/dashboard-providers/full:ro
      - ./grafana/provisioning/dashboards-prometheus-only:/etc/bioetl-grafana/dashboard-providers/prometheus-only:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards-prometheus-only:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards-prometheus-only:ro
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "/usr/local/bin/bioetl-bootstrap-grafana.sh"]
    # Renderer optional: do not health-gate Grafana on Chromium (was 180s wait).
    depends_on:
      prometheus:
        condition: service_healthy
      pushgateway:
        condition: service_started
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD",
          "wget",
          "--quiet",
          "--tries=1",
          "--spider",
          "http://localhost:3000/api/health",
        ]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 15s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 120s
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    networks:
      - monitoring
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Local dashboards + Infinity; 7.5g was over-budget on 32 GiB hosts.
    mem_limit: 2g
    mem_reservation: 384m
    cpus: 1.0
    pids_limit: 1280
    init: true
    stop_grace_period: 120s
    logging:
      { driver: json-file, options: { max-size: "200m", max-file: "10" } }

  # Chromium renders are memory-heavy. Previous defaults (mem 15g + concurrency 2)
  # allowed ~15–30g peaks with Grafana on 32 GiB hosts. Local budget: 1 browser
  # at a time, cgroup 3g.
  #
  # /dev/shm policy (do not mix):
  # - Default: real /dev/shm via shm_size=512mb, NO --disable-dev-shm-usage.
  #   Pairing disable-dev-shm-usage with a large shm_size (e.g. 2gb) wastes host
  #   shared memory while Chromium still spills to /tmp under load → thrash.
  # - Low-shm hosts only: set BROWSER_FLAGS with --disable-dev-shm-usage and
  #   drop shm_size to Docker default (~64mb); never keep both large shm + disable.
  renderer:
    image: grafana/grafana-image-renderer@sha256:c0c920e6974b0d30ae25313051344afcd2054362529968ebd9545a4b2bc8119b
    shm_size: "512mb"
    environment:
      - ENABLE_METRICS=true
      - HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0
      - AUTH_TOKEN=${GF_RENDERING_RENDERER_TOKEN:?GF_RENDERING_RENDERER_TOKEN is required}
      # No --disable-dev-shm-usage: matches shm_size above (single-tab local budget).
      # Do not pair --disable-gpu with --disable-software-rasterizer: Chromium then
      # has no raster backend and chromedp dies with "websocket url timeout reached".
      - BROWSER_FLAGS=${GRAFANA_IMAGE_RENDERER_BROWSER_FLAGS:---no-sandbox,--disable-gpu,--js-flags=--max-old-space-size=512}
      # chromedp default 20s is too short after renderer recreate on Desktop.
      - BROWSER_WS_URL_READ_TIMEOUT=${GRAFANA_IMAGE_RENDERER_WS_URL_READ_TIMEOUT:-90s}
      - BROWSER_READINESS_TIMEOUT=${GRAFANA_IMAGE_RENDERER_READINESS_TIMEOUT:-120s}
      # Table d-solo never reaches network-idle (Grafana Live / Infinity). Skip
      # that wait; cap query-ready so capture happens after first data paint.
      - BROWSER_READINESS_DISABLE_NETWORK_WAIT=${GRAFANA_IMAGE_RENDERER_DISABLE_NETWORK_WAIT:-true}
      - BROWSER_READINESS_GIVE_UP_ON_ALL_QUERIES=${GRAFANA_IMAGE_RENDERER_GIVE_UP_ON_ALL_QUERIES:-12s}
      - RENDERING_MODE=${GRAFANA_IMAGE_RENDERER_MODE:-default}
      - RENDERING_CLUSTERING_MODE=${GRAFANA_IMAGE_RENDERER_CLUSTERING_MODE:-browser}
      # Serial renders by default (was 2). Override only on high-RAM audit hosts.
      - RENDERING_CLUSTERING_MAX_CONCURRENCY=${GRAFANA_IMAGE_RENDERER_MAX_CONCURRENCY:-1}
      - GOMEMLIMIT=${GRAFANA_IMAGE_RENDERER_GOMEMLIMIT:-1GiB}
    networks:
      - monitoring
    # Recovery: bounded restarts after OOM/crash; stay down after 3 failures so
    # Grafana is not hammered by a flapping Chromium (operator restarts via
    # scripts/ops/observability/grafana/recover_renderer.ps1|.sh).
    restart: on-failure:3
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "grafana-image-renderer", "healthcheck"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 15s
      retries: 10
      # Was 180s and inflated operator "stack ready" when renderer was required.
      # Optional service: short grace; screenshots retry if still warming.
      start_period: 45s
    # Peak ≈ one Chromium tab + Go process; hard cap prevents 15g runaway.
    # Highest score among monitoring services → kernel prefers this victim first.
    oom_score_adj: 800
    mem_limit: 3g
    memswap_limit: 3g
    mem_reservation: 512m
    cpus: 1.0
    pids_limit: 1024
    init: true
    stop_grace_period: 120s
    logging:
      { driver: json-file, options: { max-size: "100m", max-file: "10" } }

volumes:
  prometheus-data:
  grafana-data:
  pushgateway-data:

networks:
  # Shared fixed name across main + monitoring projects.
  # external:true — created by runtime_manager ensure-networks / check --ensure
  # (owner label com.bioetl.owner). Avoids Compose label clash when the net
  # already exists from another project (main) or ensure-networks.
  # bioetl-runtime is NOT required here (main/neo4j only).
  # Scrape/Ops HTTP still need container `bioetl` attached to this network.
  monitoring:
    name: bioetl-monitoring
    external: true
